open_questions: Find a transcription of a record that shows his five over four as played: the books' videos demonstrate it, but no transcription of a record was read.
Read Intro to Polyrhythms and Metric Modulations whole (Mel Bay): only the contents, his shop's description and Modern Drummer's review were read.
Charette's 'All of You puts 5 over 4': a 5/4 laid over the 4/4, or quintuplets? Read as two meters ('swings hard in both'), not confirmed.
The note value of the long groups of five in Rhythm-a-ning's bridge (DIY-Drummer does not say).
Measured tempos for Moment's Notice, All of You, All the Things You Are, Rhythm-a-ning and Guernsey St. Gooseneck.
His Modern Drummer columns and interviews, read whole.

identity.name: Ari Hoenig
identity.summary: A New York jazz drummer from Philadelphia, leader of Punk Bop and his trios, and for years the drummer with Jean-Michel Pilc and Kenny Werner. He bends bar lines and implies other time signatures over a tune's form without losing it, by a method he wrote down with the bassist Johannes Weidenmueller in Intro to Polyrhythms and Metric Modulations: quarter-note triplets, dotted quarters, fives and sevens, five over four, metric modulation. He also plays melodies on the kit, pitching the drums with an elbow or hand on the head.

traditions.impact: His father a conductor and classical singer, his mother a violinist and pianist; violin and piano from six, drums from twelve.
Playing with young jazz musicians at Philadelphia clubs from fourteen; later the organist Shirley Scott.

traditions.tradition: Punk, hardcore, metal, funk and hip-hop
traditions.impact: Listened to as a boy; the name Punk Bop is for a bebop band 'capable of changing directions at any time'.

formative_events.event: Three years at the University of North Texas, studying with Ed Soph and playing in the One O'Clock Lab Band; then William Paterson College from 1995.
Formed his quartet with Jacques Schwarz-Bart, Jean-Michel Pilc and Matt Penman, Mondays at Fat Cat.

eras.label: Pilc, Werner and the solo records
eras.context: Sideman with Jean-Michel Pilc, Kenny Werner and Richard Bona; two solo kit albums, Time Travels and The Life of a Day; his quartet's The Painter.

eras.label: Dreyfus, Punk Bop and the books
eras.context: Inversations, Bert's Playground and Lines of Oppression; Intro to Polyrhythms (2009) and Metric Modulations (2012) with Johannes Weidenmueller.

eras.label: Fresh Sound trios and standards
eras.context: The Pauper and the Magician, NY Standard, Conner's Days, Golden Treasures and Tea for Three.

evidence.note: No source describes where he places the beat.

swing.notes: An estimate; no measurement found. His standards run from 90 to 285 (AllSolos).

dynamics.balance: Light and exact ('a wonderfully exquisite touch', All About Jazz), with bursts of force.

feel_profile.interaction: Changes the rhythm at intervals, turning its emphasis round or subdividing it and making it follow the melody (Ratliff); his trios move in and out of the time shifts with him.

hand_techniques.name: Melodic drumming
hand_techniques.description: Melodies played on the kit at their pitches: the drums tuned across about an octave, a head pressed with the elbow or hand to bend its pitch, as on Anthropology, 'Round Midnight and Moanin'.

hand_techniques.name: Comping that stresses the middle triplet
hand_techniques.description: Systems Book 1 teaches jazz comping with melodies that stress the second note of the triplet, and triplet displacements.

foot_techniques.name: Bass drum under a melody
foot_techniques.description: Comping on the bass drum while the toms play the tune (This Little Light of Mine).

devices.description: Takes a new tempo from a subdivision of the old inside a tune's form, and back: the subject of Metric Modulations: Contracting and Expanding Time Within Form (Mel Bay, 2012), written with Johannes Weidenmueller and demonstrated by them in duo and trio.

evidence.note: Modern Drummer ties the books to how he plays with his band, Werner and Pilc: 'a very specific method to his madness'. Charette calls him 'a master of metric modulation'. No modulation is located in a particular record's bars.

devices.description: Implies another time signature over the tune's own while the band keeps the form ('implying alternate time signatures without ever losing track of the form'); on All of You, five laid over four.

evidence.note: Charette: 'All of You puts 5 over 4 and swings hard in both', read here as 5/4 over 4/4; he does not say which.

devices.description: Five- and seven-note groupings, in eighth notes and in triplets, run across the bar line until they come round; Rhythm-a-ning's bridge is phrased in long groups of five, starting on the last beat before the bridge.

evidence.note: The fives and sevens are Metric Modulations' material (Modern Drummer); the Rhythm-a-ning bridge is from a drummer's transcription notes, with no note value given.

devices.description: Quarter-note triplets in 4/4, three in the time of two beats: one of the 'core rhythms' of implied time in Intro to Polyrhythms.

evidence.note: From the book's contents ('Quarter-Note Triplets in 4/4') and Modern Drummer's account of it; no record's bars read.

devices.description: Dotted quarters in 4/4, two in the time of three beats: another core rhythm of implied time in Intro to Polyrhythms.

evidence.note: From the book's contents ('Dotted Quarter Notes in 4/4'); no record's bars read.

devices.description: Dotted quarters in 3/4: two even beats over the bar of three in a waltz.

evidence.note: From the book's contents ('Dotted Quarter Notes in 3/4'); no record's bars read.

devices.description: Five over four: five even notes in the time of four beats, a tuplet the sixteenth grid cannot hold, taught in Metric Modulations and played by him in its improvised examples.

evidence.note: Modern Drummer lists 'five-over-four polyrhythms' in Vol. 2; his shop says its DVD has improvised examples by him in duo and trio. No transcription of a record with it was read.

devices.description: A figure moved by a subdivision: the four-bar tag of The Way You Look Tonight 'becomes fodder for rhythmic displacement'; triplet displacements in Systems Book 1.
examples: The Way You Look Tonight (Bert's Playground, 2008)

searched: Modern Drummer review of Metric Modulations Vol. 2 (2012)
Intro to Polyrhythms contents (Guitar Solo Publications) and his Bandcamp shop
All About Jazz: reviews of Inversations, Bert's Playground, Lines of Oppression, The Pauper and the Magician; Orthmann on the solo records; the Bert's Playground release
JazzTimes: Lines of Oppression; Punk Bop: Live at Smalls
Fresh Sound pages for NY Standard, Conner's Days, Golden Treasures and Tea for Three, with their press
DIY-Drummer blog on Lines of Oppression
WBGO (2017); The New York Times (Ratliff); This is Jazz (2025); The Drum Click (2025); Learn Jazz Standards (2014)
Songsterr (no Hoenig tabs); YouTube transcriptions of his Anthropology solo and 'Rhythm' (titles only; the notation could not be read)
devices_search.note: Eight devices, all but metric modulation 'likely': most come from his books' contents and Modern Drummer's review, which ties them to how he plays, rather than from a transcription of a record. Odd meters are not devices: Moment's Notice in 7/8, Fall and All the Things You Are in 5/4, Arrows and Loops and Figuration in eleven. New Found Innocence is 'multi-time signature' (All About Jazz): a meter change, not tagged. Not used: copies of the books on file-sharing sites.

voice_language.hihat: The foot on 2 and 4 under the ride; a partly open hat struck for a light hiss (Orthmann).
voice_language.snare: Single strokes, buzzes and stick shots; snares off for a melody; the elbow on the head to bend its pitch.
voice_language.kick: Punctuation more than a constant, and a comping voice under a tom melody.
voice_language.toms: Tuned to pitches: the melody instrument.
voice_language.cymbals: Struck to match the phrase, not to mark it.

implements.notes: Brushes on ballads; mallets and bare hands for melodies (Moanin').

aesthetic: a small four-piece kit with the drums tuned to pitches

sample_hints.tool: A four-piece jazz kit, toms tuned melodically, a ride and a hi-hat.

signature_traits.label: Bar lines bent, the form kept
signature_traits.description: He implies other time signatures and tempos over a tune's form, so he can sound as though he has left the time, and comes back on the form.

signature_traits.label: Melodies on the kit
signature_traits.description: Plays a tune's melody at its pitches on toms and snare, the heads bent with an elbow or hand: Anthropology, 'Round Midnight, Moanin', This Little Light of Mine.

signature_traits.label: Standards in other meters
signature_traits.description: Standards rearranged into odd meters: Moment's Notice in 7/8, Fall and All the Things You Are in 5/4.

patterns.name: Quarter-note triplets over the swing
patterns.function: Implied time: three in the time of two beats on the snare and toms while the ride and foot keep 4/4

evidence.note: Illustrates the 'core rhythm' of Intro to Polyrhythms; not a quote.

cross_rhythms.description: Quarter-note triplets: three in the time of two beats.

patterns.name: Fives of triplets across the bar
patterns.function: A five-triplet cell accented on the snare and kick until it comes round, under the ride

evidence.note: Illustrates Metric Modulations' five-note groupings in triplets; not a quote.

licks_described.name: A melody on the toms
licks_described.description: A tune's melody at its pitches on the toms and snare, the heads bent with the elbow, over a bass drum comp.

licks_described.name: Rhythm-a-ning's bridge in fives
licks_described.description: The bridge melody phrased in long groups of five, from the last beat before the bridge.

equipment.label: Four-piece jazz kit
equipment.layout_notes: A conventional four-piece kit and a few cymbals, no percussion, the drums tuned for melodies.

evidence.note: Nefertiti among the five records that shaped him.
The Jo Jones Trio among his five records.

aspects: co-author of Intro to Polyrhythms and Metric Modulations

books.title: Intro to Polyrhythms (with Johannes Weidenmueller)
books.summary: Implied time from core rhythms: eighth-note triplets, eighth notes, quarter-note triplets in 4/4, dotted quarters in 3/4 and 4/4; for any instrument, with video.

books.title: Metric Modulations: Contracting and Expanding Time Within Form, Vol. 2 (with Johannes Weidenmueller)
books.summary: Metric modulation, implied time in odd meters, fives and sevens in eighths and triplets, five over four; improvised examples in duo and trio.

books.title: Systems Book 1: Drumming Technique and Melodic Jazz Independence
books.summary: Four-way coordination, comping that stresses the second triplet, triplet displacements.

philosophy.idea: Learn songs, a great many of them: that is what he practised most.
See, sing and hear the subdivisions and their groupings, whatever the instrument.

innovations: A written method for implied time and metric modulation inside standard forms
Melodies at pitch on a four-piece kit
common_misconceptions: That he leaves the time at random: the bar lines bend by a method, and the form is kept (Modern Drummer).

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: Open jazz kit, toms tuned to pitches
generation_rules: Each song in its own meter and tempo: swing in triplets or eighths, a waltz, 7/8, 5/4, a hip-hop groove.
The hi-hat foot on 2 and 4 under the ride; comping that leans on the middle triplet.
Phrase ends laid over the time: fives and sevens across the bar, quarter-note triplets, dotted quarters, five over four, landing on the 1.
avoid: Rock backbeats in the swing songs
Melodies at pitch, which the grid cannot hold

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: A Philadelphia drummer who picks Tony Williams and Jo Jones among his records, wrote down how to bend the bar line, and plays tunes on the toms.
